records.claim: Studies of clotrimazole used on the skin or in the vagina during pregnancy have not found an increased chance of birth defects. Topical medications typically enter the body in lower amounts than when taken by mouth (oral medication). This means less medication would reach the developing fetus. Since topical clotrimazole is not well absorbed, it is unlikely to increase risks to a pregnancy.
